topic: Legal Skills: Replacing Lawyers with Markdown Files

key_points: Public executable playbook for U.S. utility-patent work: SKILL.md files, checklists, examiner/adversary protocols, intake questionnaires, and deterministic Python.
Goal is to displace legal fees, not assist counsel: a 316-item pre-filing audit, simulated USPTO prosecution loop, and adversarial design-around attack without opening a matter.
Three skills run in order: patent-audit (316-item checklist), patent-examine (recurrent simulated USPTO examination), patent-workaround (adversarial design-around testing).
Frames patent work as a document pipeline that firms wrap in scarcity, letterhead, and a rate card; the repo unwraps it.
Heavy 'not legal advice' disclaimer: skills do not file, sign, or appear before any tribunal; some acts stay reserved to a registered practitioner.
Deterministic Python scripts exist because models cannot count, do date arithmetic, or exhaustively cross-reference.
Korean legislation managed as a Git repository: each law is a Markdown file, each revision is a Git commit with the real promulgation date.
1,518 stars — demonstrates the 'legislation as code' pattern applied to Korean law.
Versioned, diffable, auditable legal text as the core value proposition.
Spanish legislation in Markdown, versioned as git: every law is a file, every reform a commit.
1,879 stars — the largest of the legalize family.
Shows the pattern scales across jurisdictions (ES, KR, GR, and the core legalize-dev/legalize at 273 stars).
Show HN: write complex legal contracts in Markdown.
Markdown as the authoring format for contracts, with structured output.
Positioned as a tool for drafting, not just reading, legal documents.
Show HN: Git-friendly legal docs with Markdown and helpers.
Emphasizes version control and collaboration on legal documents.
Complements the 'markdown for lawyers' movement with tooling.

stats.fact: Legal's AI repricing is estimated at a $900B market ('Death of the Billable Hour: Legal's $900B AI Repricing').
stats.source: Substack / Death of the Billable Hour

stats.fact: Drafting and filing a U.S. utility patent application can cost ~$18,000 at a firm; the legal-skills repo offers a checkout-and-run alternative.
A patent boutique associate is billed at roughly $400/hour for reading a draft once.
The patent-audit skill runs a 316-item pre-filing checklist: 105 blocking items, 28 mechanical (code), 169 assisted (model + evidence), 119 judgment.
legalize-es (Spanish legislation as Markdown in git) has 1,879 GitHub stars; legalize-kr (Korean) has 1,518 stars.
Common Paper (YC W23), which standardizes commercial contracts (SAFEs), drew 431 points on Hacker News at launch.
The 'Markdown for Lawyers' idea dates to at least 2016, separating lawyerly content from typesetting.

angles: Process belongs in files, not firms: most of what clients pay for is process, and process belongs in versioned markdown.
Agent skills (SKILL.md) as executable legal playbooks — the model follows a contract, not a vibe.
Legislation as code: versioned, diffable, auditable law in git (legalize family across ES/KR/GR).
Deterministic checks keep LLMs honest: models can't count, do date arithmetic, or exhaustively cross-reference, so Python scripts enforce the mechanical parts.
The 'not legal advice' boundary: what stays reserved to registered practitioners (signing, filing, duty-of-candor calls).
Cost displacement: an $18k filing vs a repo checkout and a model that costs less than lunch.
The billable-hour model is being repriced by AI — a $900B market shift.
